P0208.title: Open problem: Extremal arc-transitive walk parameters away from cycles
P0208.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status candidate_full_solution). On arc-transitive n-vertex graphs other than n-cycles, are maximal commute time O(n log n), relaxation time O(n), and the maximal-commute to twice stationary-average-hitting ratio asymptotic to1? Source: Aldous-Fill: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, 2002 recompiled2014, Open Problem7.27, PDFp259; definitionp254. Status notes: Focused primary searches2026-09-06 found source question and related established results, but no verified later disposition. Absence from search is not proof of current openness or novelty.
Posed in Aldous-Fill: Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, 2002 recompiled2014
Status as recorded in the campaign ledger on 2026-09-07

P0458.title: Open problem: The standardized degree law in growing bilateral preference graphs
P0458.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status candidate_partial_counterexample). Determine the limiting law of (D-E[D])/sqrt(Var(D)) for a typical LK(n,k) degree as the preference budget grows. Source: Dabirian and Subramanian: Connectivity of a family of bilateral preference random graphs, Open Problems; PDF3 first additional question. Status notes: 2026-09-07 bounded primary searches for EWT, La-Kabkab and bilateral preference degree results; 2025 connectivity theorem credited. No current-open or novelty certification.

Status as recorded in the campaign ledger on 2026-09-07

C0129.title: Open problem: Recurrence-transience criterion for excited random walks under stationary ergodic environments
C0129.body:

P0087.title: Open problem: Forced network urn convergence and diffusion scaling
P0087.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For Z_(n+1)=(1-r-f)Z_n+r X_(n+1)+f p with E[X_(n+1)|F_n]=Q Z_n, Q=A^T irreducible row-stochastic and X binary coordinatewise, determine nonconvergence and the continuous-time limit when r tends to0 and f is asymptotic to c r^2. C0020.title: Open problem: Optimal exponent for the computational complexity of randomised algorithms for percolation crossings
C0020.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Find the smallest sigma such that there are randomised algorithms A_n deciding the left-right crossing f_n of an n x n box in critical percolation with computational complexity C(A_n) <= n^sigma; known sigma in [6/4, 7/4]. Source: Garban and Steif: Noise sensitivity of Boolean functions and percolation, lecture notes with open problems, Chapter VIII Section 4, p. 92.
Posed in Garban and Steif: Noise sensitivity of Boolean functions and percolation, lecture notes with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

C0074.title: Open problem: Scaling limit of random walk on the high-dimensional incipient infinite cluster
C0074.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Prove that random walk on the incipient infinite cluster of high-dimensional (d > 6) percolation has a non-degenerate scaling limit. Source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems, Open Problem 14.2, p. 212. Status notes: Ben Arous, Cabezas and Fribergh ('Scaling limit for the ant in high-dimensional labyrinths', CPAM 2019) proved a scaling limit for random walk on high-dimensional critical clusters in the oriented and branching-random-walk settings; whether the unoriented IIC case d > 6 is covered was not confirmed in this session.
Posed in Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

C0116.title: Open problem: Deterministic (1+epsilon)-approximation of the cover time
C0116.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). Is there, for every epsilon > 0, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm approximating the cover time t_cov(G) of a graph within a factor 1 + epsilon? (Known for trees by Feige-Zeitouni; constant-factor approximation by Ding-Lee-Peres.) Source: Ding, Lee, Peres: Cover times, blanket times and majorizing measures, Ann. Math. 2012, with open questions, Question 5.1, p. 51.
Posed in Ding, Lee, Peres: Cover times, blanket times and majorizing measures, Ann. Math. 2012, with open questions

P0034.title: Open problem: Recurrence of the planar horizontal-new vertical-old walk
P0034.body:
